concept: Judiciary, Changes in Indian Administration after 1858
question: In 1862, the High Court was first established at:
solution:
The correct answer is **__Madras.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Bombay High Court and the Madras High Court were established on Aug 14 and 26th June 1862, respectively.**
 
• The Calcutta High Court was the first High Court and one of the three Chartered High Courts to be set up in India, along with the High Courts of Bombay and Madras under the **Indian High Courts Act of 1861 **passed in the British Parliament.
 
• This authorized the Crown to create High Courts in British India.
 
• The Calcutta High Court was established as the High Court of Judicature at Fort William on July 1, 1862, which was preceded by the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William.
 
• The Allahabad High Court was founded as the High Court of Judicature for the North-Western Provinces at Agra on 17 March 1866 by the **Indian High Courts Act of 1861.**
 
• The location of the High Court for the North-Western Provinces was shifted from Agra to Allahabad in 1869 and the name was correspondingly changed to the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad on 11 March 1919.
